content.jointProblem: Can an uncertainty-aware spatial data pipeline link incompletely located farm policies to hail exposure estimates and identify potentially underpriced portfolio segments more reliably than municipality-level rating? The first experiment would test whether cadastral data-cleaning and overlay methods transfer to policy–weather linkage, and whether the available five-kilometre daily weather data support any defensible field-level differentiation, using spatially and temporally held-out claims.

rationale.text: Lalić has demonstrated cadastral spatial-query benchmarking experience relevant to building and testing policy-to-parcel and parcel-to-weather overlays.

sources.quote: Query response times were measured across six spatial query types (bounding-box, point-in-polygon, distance, k-nearest-neighbour, clip, and overlay)

rationale.text: His published Python/PostGIS preprocessing work provides a concrete starting point for checking parcel geometry quality before exposure assignment.

sources.quote: This paper presents a preprocessing workflow implemented in Python using Shapely and PostGIS that automatically detects and classifies four error types

rationale.text: His project experience covers production-scale spatial data pipelines and operator-facing outputs, relevant to moving beyond manual QGIS analysis.

sources.quote: The project developed a reference pipeline covering topological error correction, coordinate precision normalisation, spatial grid partitioning, and incremental tile cache management.
Project outputs include open-source pipeline components, operator training materials, and a technical handbook for cadastral SDI administrators.

rationale.text: He has practical industry experience redesigning PostGIS schemas for cadastral data management.

sources.quote: on PostGIS schema redesign for their cadastral data management product between 2016 and 2018.

constraints.text: Field-level exposure assignment must explicitly retain location and weather-resolution uncertainty; neither settlement-only addresses nor coarse weather grids establish field-level hail intensity.

sources.quote: a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.
We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution

constraints.text: Validation must work within the available three-year, approximately 1,200-policy dataset and test against the existing municipality-level rating baseline.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.
Our current approach is to rate by municipality and apply a single hail loading per municipality

constraints.text: The deliverable must support automated pricing inputs compatible with the company's existing batch-scoring workflow, rather than stop at a map prototype.

sources.quote: turning that into something that feeds the pricing model automatically is beyond what our team can do alone.
Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh

constraints.text: Implementation and handover must accommodate a company without a dedicated research unit and with shared operational/development staff.

sources.quote: The company has no dedicated research unit
a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.

constraints.text: Scheduling must respect the stated one-engagement capacity from mid-2026 onward; actual availability remains unconfirmed.

sources.quote: His group has capacity to take on one additional contract research engagement from mid-2026 onward.

constraints.text: Data-sharing arrangements should accommodate his preference for authentic, anonymised production data under NDA.

sources.quote: He prefers industry partners who can share anonymised but authentic data under NDA.

risks: The strongest evidence concerns cadastral engineering, not hail-intensity estimation or insurance pricing. Transfer to policy–weather linkage must be tested first; meteorological and actuarial expertise may also be needed.
Five-kilometre daily weather observations may not resolve narrow, fast-moving hail tracks. More precise parcel geometries alone cannot create missing meteorological information.
Settlement-level policy addresses may remain ambiguous even where loss records are geo-tagged; claim locations may not identify every insured field or building.
Three summers may contain too few independent storms for stable out-of-sample conclusions. Claims-only or incomplete exposure records could bias apparent underpricing.
The reported excess claim cost does not establish that hail exposure is its cause; coverage, insured values and other loss drivers require examination.
Integration could stall under operational workload, as the company's earlier flood-mapping prototype was completed but not integrated into pricing.
Current researcher availability, project budget, delivery deadline, data licences and company commitment of staff remain unknown.
questions: Can Lalić confirm current availability for a joint project, the earliest start date and staff allocation within the one-engagement capacity?
What budget, deadline, company technical owner and actuarial owner can be committed?
Can the company provide all insured exposures, including non-claiming policies, policy periods, sums insured, coverage terms, claim dates and loss amounts?
What do the loss geotags represent, and can settlement-only policy records be linked to verified parcel identifiers, field boundaries or insured-building coordinates?

Which hail-related variables, timestamps, uncertainty estimates and historical coverage does MeteoVoj provide? Are radar or other independent event observations available if the initial resolution test fails?
Can policy, cadastral and weather data be shared and linked under suitable licences and an NDA, with anonymisation that preserves necessary spatial relationships?
Who will supply meteorological and actuarial expertise, and what held-out validation criteria would justify using an exposure factor rather than retaining municipality-level rating?
What deployment interfaces, database extensions, access controls and audit requirements apply, and who will maintain the pipeline after handover?
